original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-jacobson}
A ring $R$ is Jacobson if and only if $\Spec(R)$
is Jacobson, see Topology,
Definition \ref{topology-definition-space-jacobson}.
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with identity. Then $R$ is Jacobson (every radical ideal is the intersection of maximal ideals containing it) if and only if $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ is a Jacobson topological space (every closed subset is the closure of its closed points).
hypotheses: $R$ is a commutative ring with identity.
conclusions: $R$ is Jacobson if and only if every closed subset of $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ has dense closed points.
semantic_review_note: Resolved topology-definition-space-jacobson directly: closed points dense in each closed subspace. Ring Jacobson and spectral-space Jacobson are equivalent conditions, not unconditional assertions. Both definitions made explicit.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-characterize-jacobson}
Let $R$ be a ring. If $R$ is not Jacobson there exist
a prime $\mathfrak p \subset R$, an element $f \in R$
such that the following hold
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathfrak p$ is not a maximal ideal,
\item $f \not \in \mathfrak p$,
\item $V(\mathfrak p) \cap D(f) = \{\mathfrak p\}$, and
\item $(R/\mathfrak p)_f$ is a field.
\end{enumerate}
On the other hand, if $R$ is Jacobson, then for any pair $(\mathfrak p, f)$
such that (1) and (2) hold the set $V(\mathfrak p) \cap D(f)$ is
infinite.

such that the following hold
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathfrak p$ is not a maximal ideal,
\item $f \not \in \mathfrak p$,
\item $V(\mathfrak p) \cap D(f) = \{\mathfrak p\}$, and
\item $(R/\mathfrak p)_f$ is a field.
\end{enumerate}
On the other hand, if $R$ is Jacobson, then for any pair $(\mathfrak p, f)$
such that (1) and (2) hold the set $V(\mathfrak p) \cap D(f)$ is
infinite.
hypotheses: $R$ is a commutative ring with identity.
conclusions: If $R$ is not Jacobson, there exist a prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ and $f\in R$ such that $\mathfrak p$ is not maximal, $f\notin\mathfrak p$, $V(\mathfrak p)\cap D(f)=\{\mathfrak p\}$, and $(R/\mathfrak p)_f$ is a field.
If $R$ is Jacobson, for every nonmaximal prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ and every $f\notin\mathfrak p$, the set $V(\mathfrak p)\cap D(f)$ is infinite.

\begin{enumerate}

is finite.

\label{lemma-image-finite-type-map-Jacobson-rings}
Let $R \to S$ be a finite type ring map of Jacobson rings.
Denote $X = \Spec(R)$ and $Y = \Spec(S)$.
Write $f : Y \to X$ the induced
map of spectra. Let $E \subset Y = \Spec(S)$ be a
constructible set. Denote with a subscript ${}_0$ the set
of closed points of a topological space.
\begin{enumerate}
\item We have $f(E)_0 = f(E_0) = X_0 \cap f(E)$.
\item A point $\xi \in X$ is in $f(E)$ if and only if
$\overline{\{\xi\}} \cap f(E_0)$ is dense in $\overline{\{\xi\}}$.
\end{enumerate}

is a short exact sequence of $R$-modules.
